scheme_name: Raja Harishachandra Shramik Mratak Antyeshti Sahayata Yojana
description:
The Raja Harishachandra Shramik Mratak Antyeshti Sahayata Yojana is a welfare scheme initiated by the Government of Maharashtra in India. 

This scheme was launched on 1st January 2018. 

It aims to provide financial assistance for the last rites of unorganized sector workers who pass away. 

The initiative is named after Raja Harishchandra, a legendary king known for his commitment to truth and justice. 

The scheme recognizes the hardships faced by the families of deceased workers in arranging for funerals. 

The primary objective of the scheme is to alleviate the financial burden on the families during a time of grief. 

The government aims to ensure that every unorganized worker receives dignified last rites. 

Under this scheme, a financial assistance of ₹10,000 is provided to the family of the deceased worker. 

This amount is intended to cover the expenses associated with the last rites and funeral arrangements. 

The scheme specifically targets workers in the unorganized sector, which constitutes a significant portion of the workforce in Maharashtra. 

According to the 2011 Census, approximately 94% of the Indian workforce is employed in the unorganized sector. 

The eligibility criteria for this scheme are clearly defined. 

The applicant must be a resident of Maharashtra. 

The deceased must have been an unorganized sector worker. 

The worker should have been registered under the Maharashtra Unorganized Workers Social Security Act, 2008. 

There are no specific age limits for the deceased worker. 

However, the family must provide proof of the worker's employment in the unorganized sector. 

The application process for the Raja Harishachandra Shramik Mratak Antyeshti Sahayata Yojana is straightforward. 

The applicant must fill out a prescribed application form. 

This form can be obtained from the local Gram Panchayat office or online through the Maharashtra government’s official website. 

Along with the application form, the following documents are required: 

A copy of the death certificate of the deceased worker. 

Proof of the deceased's employment in the unorganized sector. 

Aadhar card or any other government-issued identity proof of the applicant. 

Bank account details of the applicant for fund transfer. 

Once the application is complete with all required documents, it should be submitted to the local authority. 

The local authority is typically the Gram Panchayat or the Municipal Corporation, depending on the area of residence. 

After submission, the application will be verified by the concerned officials. 

The verification process usually takes about 15 days. 

Upon successful verification, the financial assistance will be disbursed. 

The amount is transferred directly to the bank account of the applicant. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Labour, Government of Maharashtra. 

The contact details for the Department of Labour can be found on the official Maharashtra government website. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to improve the social security framework for unorganized workers in the state. 

The government has recognized the need for such welfare measures due to the vulnerability of unorganized workers. 

In Maharashtra, there are approximately 10 crore unorganized workers, highlighting the scale of the issue. 

The Raja Harishachandra Shramik Mratak Antyeshti Sahayata Yojana is a crucial step in providing support to these workers' families. 

The scheme also reflects the government's commitment to ensuring dignity in death for all workers. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme aims to create awareness about the rights and benefits available to unorganized workers. 

The government has conducted various outreach programs to educate workers about this scheme. 

These programs are aimed at ensuring that eligible families are aware of the assistance available to them. 

The scheme has received positive feedback from beneficiaries who have utilized the funds for last rites. 

It has been reported that the scheme has helped thousands of families since its inception. 

The financial assistance has enabled families to perform the last rites without incurring debt. 

This is particularly important in a society where funeral expenses can be a significant financial burden. 

The Raja Harishachandra Shramik Mratak Antyeshti Sahayata Yojana is part of a larger framework of social security initiatives in Maharashtra. 

The government continues to explore ways to expand and enhance support for unorganized workers. 

The scheme has been instrumental in addressing the immediate needs of families in distress. 

The government is committed to ensuring that no family is left to fend for themselves during such difficult times. 

The Raja Harishachandra Shramik Mratak Antyeshti Sahayata Yojana is a testament to this commitment. 

In conclusion, this scheme provides essential support to the families of unorganized workers in Maharashtra. 

It ensures that they receive the necessary financial assistance for last rites. 

The scheme is a significant step towards improving the welfare of unorganized workers and their families. 

It reflects the government's dedication to social justice and support for the vulnerable sections of society. 

The Raja Harishachandra Shramik Mratak Antyeshti Sahayata Yojana is a crucial initiative that aims to provide dignity in death. 

It is an essential part of the social security landscape in Maharashtra. 

The scheme continues to evolve and adapt to the needs of the workforce. 

The government remains focused on enhancing the welfare of unorganized workers through various initiatives. 

The Raja Harishachandra Shramik Mratak Antyeshti Sahayata Yojana is a vital component of this broader vision.
